title: Singapore charges three in Nvidia server fraud case
description: Singapore charged Aaron Woon, Alan Wei and Li Ming with fraud over Dell and Supermicro server deals worth about US$390M, linked to suspected movement of Nvidia chips. Corporate charges against Aperia Group firms followed in July 2026.
significance: Opened the first public diversion case touching the Singapore to Malaysia server corridor.

title: Malaysia vows action after Singapore says servers may have gone to Malaysia
description: After Singapore's law minister said the Dell and Supermicro servers may have moved on to Malaysia, MITI said it would establish whether Malaysian laws were breached. NationGate shares fell by the 30% daily limit.
significance: First time Malaysia's data centre boom was publicly tied to chip diversion risk.

title: US asks Malaysia to monitor every Nvidia chip shipment
description: Trade minister Tengku Zafrul said the US wants Malaysia to monitor every shipment involving Nvidia chips, and set up a task force to tighten data centre rules. Malaysia's own probe of the Singapore servers found no evidence.
significance: Made US pressure on Malaysia explicit and on the record.

title: US rescinds AI Diffusion Rule and issues diversion guidance
description: BIS said it would not enforce the Biden-era tiered caps and would replace them, and issued guidance on Huawei Ascend chips, training Chinese models and diversion red flags. Its release also lists added licence requirements for Malaysia and Thailand, but no such rule was found.
significance: Lifted the planned cap on Tier 2 countries like Malaysia while shifting to case-based enforcement.

title: Report: US drafts AI chip curbs on Malaysia and Thailand
description: Bloomberg reported a draft Commerce rule to restrict Nvidia-class AI chip shipments to Malaysia and Thailand to stop diversion to China. The rule was not finalised.
significance: Showed Malaysia could be singled out despite the end of the tier system.

title: Malaysia requires permits for US-origin AI chip exports
description: MITI made all exports, transhipments and transits of high-performance US-origin AI chips subject to a Strategic Trade Permit under the Strategic Trade Act 2010, effective immediately.
significance: Malaysia's main pre-emptive move to avoid US curbs and close its transit loophole.

title: NYT: Megaspeed's Malaysian unit was set to buy about US$2B of Nvidia chips
description: The New York Times reported that Speedmatrix, the Johor unit of Singapore-based Megaspeed, received over 200 shipments of restricted Nvidia hardware from June 2024 to June 2025, and that US and Singapore authorities were probing it.
significance: Put a Johor data centre at the centre of the US diversion investigation.

title: US-Malaysia trade deal commits Malaysia to US export controls
description: Under Article 5.2 of the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade signed in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia agreed to align with US unilateral export controls and ensure its companies do not undermine them.
actor: Governments of Malaysia and the United States
significance: Turned export-control alignment into a treaty-style trade commitment.

title: US charges four over Nvidia GPUs routed via Malaysia and Thailand
description: The DOJ charged four men with exporting 400 Nvidia A100 GPUs to China via Malaysia and Thailand, and with attempting to ship H100 systems and H200 GPUs that were intercepted.
significance: Named Malaysia as a transit point in a US criminal case.

title: Bloomberg: Megaspeed imported at least US$4.6B of Nvidia hardware
description: Malaysian and Indonesian customs data showed Megaspeed units imported about 136,000 Nvidia GPUs worth at least US$4.6B since 2023, with Alibaba named as a key customer. Megaspeed and Nvidia denied diversion.
significance: Sized the scale of China-linked compute sitting in Malaysian data centres.

title: Bain's Bridge Data Centres drops Megaspeed in Malaysia
description: Bridge Data Centres told lenders in February 2026 that Zenlayer had replaced Megaspeed for all 68.4MW earmarked at its Malaysian hub, Megaspeed's largest site.
significance: Showed lenders and landlords pricing in US enforcement risk.

title: BIS: China-parented firms need licences anywhere
description: BIS guidance said advanced AI chips still need a licence when the buyer is headquartered in, or has an ultimate parent in, China, another D:5 country or Macau, wherever it is located. Existing bona fide data centre operators may keep using installed chips until further notice.
significance: Closed the gap that let Chinese-owned subsidiaries in Malaysia buy chips without a licence.

title: Customs seize 72 AI servers at KLIA Free Trade Zone
description: Customs seized 72 servers with advanced AI chips worth RM52.9 million (about US$13M) in a KLIA warehouse, allegedly bound for re-export to another Asian country. Announced 26 June and probed under Section 12 of the Strategic Trade Act.
significance: First large public seizure under Malaysia's July 2025 AI chip permit regime.

title: US maps Chinese remote use of chips; Malaysia-Thailand draft shelved
description: Bloomberg reported BIS enforcement is mapping where Chinese firms rent Nvidia compute abroad, including Alibaba allegedly using chips in Malaysia via Megaspeed. Commerce reportedly shelved its draft curbs on Malaysia and Thailand.
significance: Shifted the US focus from chip shipments to remote cloud access in Malaysia.

title: US charges Californian over US$300M of servers shipped via Malaysia
description: Prosecutors allege Greg Lui's Earthmade Computer shipped about US$300M of Nvidia-based servers to China, receiving over US$176M from two Malaysian transshipment firms; 92 servers went to Kuala Lumpur.
significance: Most explicit US charge naming Malaysian firms as transshipment intermediaries.

title: Reports: Megaspeed probe stalled as GB300 imports into Malaysia surface
description: The NYT reported Commerce paused its Megaspeed probe after Nvidia's general counsel contacted agents and the DOJ took over; Bloomberg found Megaspeed imported 17,544 GB300 chips (about US$787M) into Malaysia in Nov 2025, after Nvidia says it cut the firm off.
actor: Megaspeed; Nvidia; US Commerce and DOJ
significance: Kept Malaysian data centres at the centre of a live US political scandal over chip diversion.
